Subject: EU/UK data transfer approach + SCC options

Hi Chloe,

We're finalising the DPA and need Redwood's recommendation on which SCC modules we should adopt for BrightHelm's EU and UK data flows. Key asks:
- Which SCC module(s) do you recommend given BrightHelm is the controller and Redwood will act as processor, and Redwood also routes some processing through UK-based subprocessors?
- Can you provide a DPA redline and a short evidence pack (SOC 2 snapshot, KMS/crypto description, list of subprocessors and locations)?
- Any preferences for UK addendum language or fallback clauses?

We'd appreciate a short write-up and a suggested timeline for execution — ideally a one-page summary and a tracked DPA redline. Attaching our internal SCC checklist for background.

Thanks,
Claire Harper
Head of Legal Ops
BrightHelm Health

Attachments: BrightHelm_SCC_checklist.xlsx

From: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: Recommended SCC approach for BrightHelm (draft)

Team — internal draft notes for the BrightHelm request. Please review and flag risks.

Summary recommendation (draft):
- Primary route: EU SCCs controller->processor path for BrightHelm (use the EU SCC clauses aligned with the UK Addendum where applicable). This keeps the DPA clean for BrightHelm as controller and Redwood as processor.
- Subprocessing / cross-border routing: adopt processor->processor module for any onward transfers to UK-based subprocessors (explicitly reference the list of subprocessors and include a mechanism for notice + objection).
- Fallbacks: include an explicit fallback to the UK Addendum language for UK transfers and an operational carve-out that requires additional safeguards (KMS-in-transit keys, IP allowlists by region, minimum retention controls).

Operational asks for packaging:
- Attach SOC 2 snapshot (we have a current PDF) and a one-page KMS + encryption FAQ.
- Provide an SCCs matrix mapping our typical flows (EU->US hosted inference, EU->UK for dedicated capacity, EU->US for analytics). See attached sccs-matrix-v2.xlsx.
- Draft DPA redline (attached) with tracked comments on the module mix and the subprocessors clause.

Open questions / risks:
- Does the mix of modules create ambiguity with certain EU DPAs? Laura — does this hybrid approach raise enforcement questions?
- Neha — will we need to update DPIA for BrightHelm because of the UK routing?
- Karthik — can the runtime team confirm that routing markers are logged and we can provide per-tenant host-region evidence?

Proposed timeline: 3 business days for internal sign-off, then send to BrightHelm with a suggested DocuSign path and a short call to walk through.

Attachments referenced: sccs-matrix-v2.xlsx, DPA_redline_BrightHelm_v1.docx, SOC2-snapshot.pdf

Thanks — CM
From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Recommended SCC approach for BrightHelm (draft)

Chloe / team — quick comments from legal/privacy: we are broadly comfortable with the hybrid approach but with caveats.

Key points:
- From a legal standpoint, prefer the controller->processor SCC path for the main relationship. For onward transfers to subprocessors we should either: (a) map to the processor->processor module OR (b) keep the controller->processor wording and require the customer to approve subprocessors in the DPA. Both are workable; the customer often prefers option (b) to retain visibility. BrightHelm's preference will guide final language.
- Add an explicit UK Addendum clause and ensure it is the primary fallback for UK-located processing — that will satisfy most UK DPA reviewers.
- DPIA: yes, update required if routing to UK subprocessors changes high-risk processing. Neha, please prepare a short DPIA addendum we can share with BrightHelm.
- Evidence: security should supply the KMS diagram and a signed SOC2 snapshot. Also confirm subprocessors list (region + function).

I'll prepare legal language variants (two short paragraphs) so we can A/B test with BrightHelm: one that delegates subprocessor approval, and one that requires customer consent for new subprocessors.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

- Onward transfers: for subprocessors in the UK, we recommend a processor->processor module for operational clarity OR, if BrightHelm prefers, an approval-based subprocessor clause in the DPA. We'll present both options in the redline.

Included in the package: SCCs_option_summary.pdf (one-page), DPA_redline_BrightHelm_v1.docx (tracked), sccs-matrix-v2.xlsx, SOC2-snapshot.pdf.
